VIII. QUALITY CONTROL OF AYURVEDA, SIDDHA, UNANI AND HOMOEOPATHIC
(ASU&H) DRUGS
8.1 The AYUSH system of medicine is governed by Drug and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules
1945. Enforcement provisions of Chapter IV A of the Act is responsibility of State Governments.
Establishment of State Drug Testing Laboratories is also a statutory responsibility of States under
the Act. To provide financial assistance to States for strengthening enforcement mechanism, the
Drug Quality Control was started in the Eleventh Plan.
8.2 As per the information given in the Outcome Budget 2013-14, standardization of quality
control of ASU&H drugs as per the global trends is the prime concern of the Department of AYUSH.
8.3 In reply to a question, the Department has submitted that the following steps have been
taken to strengthen the regulatory mechanisms of ASU&H drugs:–
“(A) In order to improve the regulatory and Quality Control situation of ASU&H drugs in
the country, the Department of AYSUH set up Pharmacopoeia Commission of Indian
Medicine in 2010 to oversee the development of pharmacopoeial standards of drugs
and implemented a Centrally Sponsored Scheme since Ninth Plan to strengthen the
infrastructure and functional capacity of Drug Testing Laboratories and Pharmacies
and enforcement mechanism in the States. 29 State Drug Testing Laboratories, 46
State Pharmacies and 30 State Licensing Authorities have been supported through the
Centrally Sponsored Scheme and subsidy provided to private drug manufacturing
units for improving in-house Quality Control Laboratories as per GMP requirements.
(B) Besides, following regulatory measures under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 have
been taken and Executive Orders issued to step up quality control of ASU&H drugs:–
(i) Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU&H drugs notified followed by
GMP supplementary guidelines for manufacturing of Mineral and Herbo-mineral
formulations.
(ii) Standards to be complied in the manufacture of ASU&H drugs notified.
(iii) Regulatory provision for recognition of laboratories for testing ASU drugs and
raw materials has been made under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. Joint
inspection by the representatives of Central Government and State Licensing
Authorities initiated for recognition of Drug Testing Laboratories under the
Drugs and Cosmetics Rules.
(iv) Qualifications of the State Licensing Authorities for ASU drugs notified.
(v) Standard requirement of space and scientific manpower was prescribed for
approval to be granted for carrying out testing of ASU drugs.
(vi) To improve the shelf life and quality of ASU drugs, use of excipients was
permitted in their manufacture with specific conditions and permissible limits.
(vii) Quality and safety assurance of drugs has been promoted by prescribing
permissible limits of heavy metals, aflatoxins, pesticide residue and microbial
load and issue of orders for providing reports of batch to batch testing in the
public sector procurement of ASU medicines.
(viii) Pharmacopoeial Laboratory for Indian Medicine and Homoeopathic
Pharmacopoiea Laboratory have been notified as appellate laboratories for the
purpose of testing of ASU&H drugs.

19
(ix) Development of pharmacopoeial standards of complex multiingredient ASU
formulations has been given high priority.
(x) Ban imposed on the misleading use of prefix and suffix with the names of
classical ASU medicines and the draft Rules notified.
(xi) V oluntary quality certification scheme for AYUSH products started in
collaboration with Quality Council of India.
(xii) Shelf life/date of expiry for ASU medicines was notified under Drugs and
Cosmetics Rule 161 (B) for public safety.
(xiii) Guidelines for issue of manufacturing license to various types of Patent and
Proprietary ASU drugs notified to provide clarity about the requirement of
documents in support of efficacy and safety of ASU drugs.
(xiv) Six technical officers of the Department of AYUSH have been appointed under
Drugs and Cosmetics Rules 160 E and 160 F for discharging duties of
inspection of institutions carrying out testing of ASU drugs.
(xv) Drugs and Cosmetics Rule 161 pertaining to labeling provisions has been
amended for mandatory mention of botanical names and parts of plants used
in the Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani formulations.
(xvi) Actions have been initiated on the recommendations of Ayurveda Siddha Unani
Drugs Technical Advisory Board (ASUDTAB) for regulating retail sale of ASU
drugs containing toxic raw material, development of Good Clinical Practice
Guidelines for clinical trials on ASU drugs and development of model laboratory
practices for testing of ASU drugs.
8.4 The roadmap for strengthening the quality control of ASU&H drugs in Twefth Plan aims
at enhancing the domain and scope of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme with addition of more
components and revision of funding pattern and establishment of a separate Central Drug Controller
for AYUSH.”
8.5 The Committee takes note of the steps taken by the Department for strengthening
of the regulatory mechanism of ASU&H drugs. However, the Committee is aware that
quality control and standardization of ASU&H drugs, which are mainly herbal/herbo-mineral
preparations, is very complex and different from synthetic molecules of the allopathic
system which are produced under controlled laboratory conditions. However, given the
current scenario where regulation of ASU&H drugs leaves much to be desired, the
Committee feels that strengthening and streamlining of regulatory mechanism of ASU&H
drugs needs to be speeded up. The Committee desires that the Department should accord
high priority to the task of laying down standards of quality control of ASU&H drugs by
using modern techniques.
8.6 The Department has informed that an outlay of Rs. 80.00 crore has been approved in the
Twelfth Plan for the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Quality Control of ASU&H drugs. It is
intended to revise the scheme based on its evaluation report and suggestions from stakeholders and
add new components. The given allocation is envisaged to be spent for focused outcomes in terms
of effective quality control of ASU&H drugs including strengthening of regulatory infrastructure,
mechanism and capacity in the States; improving drug manufacturing, storage and testing facilities
in public sector; implementation of regulatory capacity building initiatives; and development of
regulatory and quality control materials.

20
8.7 In reply to a question, the Department has informed that One State Drug Testing
Laboratory (DLT) and one State Ayurvedic Pharmacy have been assisted with grant-in-aid of
Rs.21.31 lakhs and Rs.43.46 lakhs respectively. Two GMP compliant private drugs manufacturing
units availed subsidy in 2012-13. The proposals of three more State DTLs and one Pharmacy
for balance grant-in-aid have been approved by the Project Screening Committee and are in
pipeline for release of funds. With the available funds and existing funding pattern of the scheme,
it is intended to support 5 DTLs, 5 Pharmacies, 5 Licensing Authorities and 6 manufacturing
units in 2013-14. However, revision of the scheme with inclusion of new components may revise
these targets.
8.8 The Committee observes that there is a separate chapter-IV A in the Drugs and
Cosmetics Act 1940 which regulates the manufacture and sale of ASU drugs. Since the
enforcement of provisions of Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules made thereunder is under
the purview of State Drug Licensing and Drug Control Authorities, the State drugs
regulatory framework has a crucial role to play in ensuring safety and quality of ASU&H
drugs. It is in this context that strengthening of State Drug Testing Laboratories which are
facing infrastructure constraints, and shortage of manpower, assumes added significance.
The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department to quickly revise the Quality
Control Scheme and its funding pattern for greater efficacy of the Scheme.
Central Drug Controller for AYUSH
8.9 The Committee has been informed that a Central Regulatory Authority for ASU&H drugs is
contemplated to be set up. The Department in a written submission has informed that the matter
of establishing Central Drug Controller for AYUSH has been constantly pursued with the
Department of Expenditure for creation of posts. Certain specific clarifications and justification for
the required posts have been provided in February, 2013. Allocation of Rs. 102 crore in Twelfth
Plan and Rs. 7.60 crore in the annual plan 2013-14 has been budgeted to undertake the
establishment of infrastructure and manpower for the Central AYUSH Drug Controller’s office.
Proposal is also being moved for acquiring additional space to accommodate the AYUSH Drug
Controller’s office.
8.10 On being asked as to why it is not desirable to let CDSCO regulate ASU drugs also, the
Department has informed that CDSCO has been basically dealing with quality control of allopathic
drugs and accordingly, the whole paraphernalia there does not have the wherewithal to effectively
regulate ASU&H drugs. The basic reason is that ASU&H drugs are distinct from allopathic drugs
in terms of philosophy, principles, concepts, standards, quality aspects, applications, numbers and
count of manufacturing units and testing requirements and they need to have different regulations.
In-spite of common Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the regulatory issues of ASU&H drugs are
not being taken care of by the Central Drugs Controller Office due to non-availability of requisite
expertise and huge workload of matters related to allopathic drugs. The idea of having a common
Central Drugs Authority with Additional Drug Controller of AYUSH had not been earlier agreed to.
However, the office of the Drug Controller General (India) was strengthened by sanctioning 175
posts for modern medicine and was renamed as Central Drugs Standards Control Organisation
(CDSCO), but no posts were sanctioned for the Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy.
It was thereafter only that in accordance with the recommendations of a high powered Committee
and ASU Drugs Consultative Committee and considering the specific regulatory requirements of
ASU&H drugs, setting up a separate Central Drugs Controller of AYUSH was found to be a
necessary requirement.
8.11 An early action may be taken to establish and appoint AYUSH Drug Controller.

21
IX. CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES FOR DEVELOPMENT OF AYUSH INDUSTRY CLUSTERS
9.1 The Scheme was introduced in the Eleventh Five year Plan with the objective for creating
Common Facility Centre (CFC) for standardization, quality assurance and control, productivity,
marketing, infrastructure and capacity building through a cluster based approach in the form of
Special Purpose V ehicle (SPV) registered company to manufacture quality drugs of Ayurveda,
Siddha and Unani.
9.2 As per the Scheme, at least 15 enterprises within radius of 50 Km. holding GMP certificate
of AYUSH Industries and each of them having minimum annual turnover of Rs. 20.00 lakhs are
eligible under the Scheme. The Government provides one time assistance as grant-in-aid upto 60%
of the project cost subject to maximum Rs. 10.00 crore. The remaining 40% amount would be
arranged by the SPV members. One testing laboratory is mandatory for each SPV/Clusters.
9.3 The Department has informed that the approved outlay for the Scheme for the Twelfth Plan
is Rs. 121.75 crore. The Eleventh Plan outlay for the scheme was Rs. 500.00 crore out of which
only Rs. 50.49 crore could actually be spent.
9.4 The Department has also informed that during the Twelfth Plan, efforts would be made to
establish at least one industry cluster in each State. It has also been informed that the Scheme,
if required, would be modified appropriately after getting the feedback of the third party evaluation
which is in progress.
9.5 The Committee notes that 9 AYUSH Industry Clusters were set up during 2012-13.
It is a matter of concern that not a single new AYUSH Industry Cluster has been set up
since then which is indicative of the tardy progress in the matter. In its 55
th Report, the
Committee had suggested that there should be at least one AYUSH industry cluster in each
State. Though the Department has assured to move in this direction there is little action
on the ground. The Committee, therefore, exhorts the Department to quickly finalize re-
designing of the Scheme and ensure that concrete progress is made towards setting up of
at least one AYUSH Industry cluster in each State which is also necessary for supply of
quality drugs at affordable prices.

11.5 The Committee in its 55
th Report, had commented upon the misleading advertisements

11.6 On being asked as to what specific action has been taken by the Department to take up
the matter of objectionable advertisements concerning AYUSH with Ministry of Information and
Broadcasting and their response in the matter, the Department has furnished the following
information:–
“As recommended by the Hon’ble Parliamentary Committee, the matter of checking
objectionable advertisements on AYUSH drugs has been taken up with Ministry of
Information & Broadcasting and Directorate of Audio-visual Publicity (DAVP) with a
request to take action as appropriate for stopping improper advertisements on AYUSH in
electronic and print media. DA VP has informed that it does not have regulatory power
over private advertisement. Press Council of India has also informed that as per the Press
Council Act, 1978 the Council enjoys statutory authority for the print media and it is
sensitive on the issue of objectionable advertisements and have norms of Journalistic
Conduct-2010. However, these guidelines carry only ethical backing as there are no
enforcement powers with the Press Council of India. The matter is being pursued with
Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The Department of AYUSH has also written to
all State Drug Licensing Authorities/Drug Controllers of AYUSH to bring instances of

notice of Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for remedial action and to take
corrective measures in preventing inappropriate advertisements in electronic and print
media including newspapers.”

matter with the authorities concerned with renewed vigour as the issue is too important for
maintaining credibility of AYUSH systems to be left unattended. The Committee desires to

OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
The Committee is concerned to note that except for the year 2010-11, the total actual
expenditure has invariably been considerably lower than Budget Estimates, particularly in
2011-12 and 2012-13. For Example, the total actual expenditure for the year 2008-09 was
Rs. 471.13 crore against Budget Estimates (BE) of Rs. 534.00 crore; for the year 2009-10,
Rs. 678.97 crore as against BE of Rs. 734.00 crore; for the year 2011-12, Rs. 611.46 crore
as against BE of 900.00 crore; and for the year 2012-13, Rs. 580.27 crore as against BE of
Rs. 990.00 crore. The Committee is not happy with this recurrent and persistent under
utilization of plan funds allocated for the Department. The Committee is constrained to
observe that such a persistent shortfall in the utilization of plan funds is indicative of fiscal
indiscipline and serious shortcoming in formulating the Budget Estimates. The Committee
in its 55
th Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department had recommended to
take measures for exercising greater fiscal prudence. However, underutilization of the funds
to the tune of Rs. 409.73 crore vis-a-vis  BE for 2012-13 indicates that the Committee’s
advice was not heeded to. The Committee, therefore, even at the cost of repetition, strongly
recommends that concrete measures be taken to exercise utmost fiscal discipline and
ensure absorption of the allocated funds. (Para 2.5)
The Committee notes that the extent of surrendered funds is substantially higher
under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (30.9% with reference to RE) than that under Central
Sector Schemes (7.8% with reference to RE). The Committee also takes note of the
remedial steps for better absorption of funds but is not impressed by the half measures
taken by the Department to overcome the sub-optimal utilization of Plan funds as it is
obvious that these efforts have not yielded the desired results. In view of the fact that the
allocations have persistently remained under-utilized in the past several years, the
Department should have undertaken a comprehensive analysis in this regard and taken
corrective measures accordingly. Now that an evaluation of all the Schemes is being done
by an independent agency, the Committee is sanguine that the corrective measures will be
initiated for ensuring optimal and judicious utilization of the budgeted funds. The
Committee recommends that the evaluation be completed in a time-bound manner. The
Committee desires to be apprised of the outcome of the independent evaluation and action
taken thereon. The Committee would also like the Department to devise ways to evaluate
the impact of its various schemes. The Committee, simultaneously, impresses upon the
Department to be more prudent in their budget formulation and project their fund
requirements in a more realistic manner after timely collection of all the information
pertaining to fund requirements from the State Governments. (Para 2.6)
The Committee notes that a provision of Rs. 1069.00 crore has been made in B.E
2013-14 on the plan side. The Committee would expect the Department to initiate concrete
measures at least from this year onwards to ensure that the sanctioned funds are
administered in a more diligent manner. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the
steps taken for more efficient deployment and utilization of the funds budgeted for 2013-14.
(Para 2.7)
The Committee also takes note of the fact that the share of AYUSH in the total
health outlay has been substantially enhanced to Rs. 10044.00 crore in the Twelfth Plan,
30

31
which is an increase of 235.47% over the actual expenditure of Eleventh Plan of Rs. 2994.00
crore. The Committee is aware that health needs of a vast and diverse country like India
cannot be met by a single healthcare system and AYUSH health care systems have a very
vital role to play in expanding the outreach of health care to the people because of their
inherent advantages in terms of diversity, modest cost, low level of technological input, etc.
Indian system of medicines and  traditional medicines should be complementary to Modern
system of Medicine. It is in this context that the Committee welcomes the enhanced
allocation of funds for AYUSH in the Twelfth Plan. The Committee also appreciates the
efforts made by the Department in getting enhanced allocation for the year 2013-14 inspite
of the fact that there was considerable underutilization of funds during the previous year
i.e. 2012-13. Persistent underutilization of funds to such extent is a serious concern for the
Committee. The Committee is also apprehensive about the utilization of such enhanced
allocation in 2013-14. Therefore, the Committee would expect the Department to put in
place a dedicated mechanism for stricter expenditure monitoring and financial discipline so
that the scarce resources do not remain locked up and surrendered later. (Para 2.8)
Pending Utilization Certificates
The Committee observes that pendency of UCs and the huge amount involved therein
have implications for further release of funds and thus impinges on the effective
implementation of the projects. Though the Department has drawn up an ambitious plan of
reducing pendency of UCs to nil, the past trends in this regard inspire little confidence. The
Committee, therefore, desires to be informed of the detailed action plan on bringing down
the pendency of UCs to nil and the success achieved so far so that a fair assessment could
be made about the efficacy of the plan. (Para 2.10)
It is a matter of serious concern for the Committee to note that the number of
pending UCs and the amount involved therein is too substantial to be ignored. Of more
serious concern is the fact that UCs dating as far back as to 2000 and 2001 are still
pending. The Committee notes with disapproval that the steps taken by the Department for
liquidation of the pending UCs are of routine nature and have not yielded the desired
results so far. The Committee would, therefore, like the Department to expedite evaluation
of the schemes and formulate appropriate remedial measures accordingly. The Committee
would also expect the Department to play a more proactive role in the capacity building of
the States so that with better absorption capacity the funds could be utilized in a more
efficient manner. The Committee would also like to reiterate its recommendation made in
its 55
th Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 26 th April, 2012 that the Department should
formulate an action plan in coordination with the State Governments for developing an
effective and efficient coordination mechanism for timely submission of UCs. This would
also speed up execution of all the projects well within the approved cost. (Para 2.13)
Utilization of Plan Allocation for North-Eastern States and Sikkim
The Committee lends its full support to the activities and budgetary provisions for
the benefit of the North-Eastern States and Sikkim. The Committee observes that it is
essential for inclusive growth that the benefits of the growth of our economy reach the
people of the distantly located North-Eastern States of the country. The Committee would,
therefore, like the Department to closely monitor the progress of various schemes in the
North-Eastern Region and ensure that the ongoing projects there are not hamstrung for
lack of funds or due to underutilization thereof. The Committee would also like to impress
upon the Department to ensure that the projects/schemes sanctioned for the North-Eastern
Region are not delayed due to lack of approvals. (Para 2.18)

32
III. Updation of Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy
The Committee is not happy to note that despite its recommendation made in its 55 th
Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department that all such information
should be made available in the public domain in an updated form on the touch of a button,
little progress seems to have been made in this regard, which is evident from the fact that
out of 23 States in respect of which information pertaining to updation of Central Register
of Indian Medicine has been made available, eight States are lagging behind in sending
updated information. As regards the Status of updation of the Central Register of
Homoeopathy, the Committee is surprised to note that in three cases, i.e. Bihar, Tamil
Nadu and Tripura, it took sixteen or more months to incorporate the information in the
Central Registers. The Committee is aware that there is a provision in the IMCC Act 1970
mandating the State Boards to submit updated registers of practitioners on the 1
st April
every year. The Committee would, therefore, like to be intimated of the impediment coming
in the way of updation of Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy despite
there being mandatory legal provisions. The matter may be taken up at the Minister level
and frequent review meetings be held. (Para 3.2)
IV. National Institutes
National Institute of Ayurveda (NlA)
The Committee observes that the NIA is inter-alia mandated to develop high
standards of teaching in Ayurvedic System of Medicine and therefore the acute shortage of
the faculty is certain to adversely affect the functioning of this premier Institute. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should take immediate measures
towards filling up vacancies in faculty posts with priority and urgency. The Committee also
observes that in pursuance of the recommendation of the Committee, the Department in its
Action Taken Note on the 55
th Report of the Committee, had assured to take action to
appoint professionally qualified persons on short-term contract or deputation basis to
overcome the staff crunch in senior faculty positions. The Committee is not aware whether
any forward movement has been made in this regard. The Committee, therefore,
recommends to the Department to take immediate action towards appointing professionally
qualified persons on short-term contract or deputation against these posts till regular
appointments are made and desires to be kept apprised of the headway made in the matter.
(Para 4.3)
National Institute of Homoeopathy (NIH)
The Committee observes that the delay in completion of projects often results in cost
overrun. The Committee would, therefore, like the Department to closely monitor the
progress of construction of Academic-cum-Library Building on a quarterly basis in order to
avoid time overrun and resultant cost escalation. (Para 4.6)
The Committee observes that the expansion of the Hospital from 100 to 250 beds was
targeted to be achieved during 2010-11. Two years have elapsed since then, but the project
is yet to completed. The time-overrun has led to cost overrun. The Committee has been
advising the Department to streamline its monitoring mechanism so that such slippages in
timely implementing the project and the resultant cost overrun could be minimized. The
Committee is constrained to observe that the delay in completion of the project is indicative
of slack monitoring and bad planning. The Committee, therefore, exhorts the Department
to pay focused attention towards expansion of the Hospital from its existsing bed strength

33
of 100 to 250 beds. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress of
implementation of the project. (Para 4.8)
The Committee expresses its concern over such a large number of vacant posts in
teaching cadre which is certain to impair the functioning of NIH. The Committee observes
that the main objective of NIH is to develop excellence in homoeopathic education and
conduct UG and PG courses. It is, therefore, imperative for the Department to urgently take
steps to fill up the vacancies in a specific time-frame. The Committee desires to be apprised
of the measures taken by the Department and progress made towards filling up all vacant
posts of NIH. (Para 4.10)
Morarji Desai National Institute of YOGA (MDNIY)
The Committee observes that one of the main factors contributing to underutilization
of the budgeted funds is delay in necessary approvals. The Committee would, therefore, like
to impress upon the Department to proactively pursue and complete all pre-approval
activities for the new schemes/additional components under the above head so that the
approved outlay for the Twelfth Plan is utilized gainfully and there are no instances of sub-
optimal utilization of the approved outlay. (Para 4.13)
The Committee, welcomes the evaluation of the Advanced Centres of Yoga by the
Scientific Advisory Committee and desires to be apprised of its findings and action taken
thereon. (Para 4.15)
North Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homeopathy (NEIAH), Shillong
The Committee notes that the proposal for establishment of NEIAH was approved by
the Cabinet on the 27
th March, 2008. More than five years have passed since then, but the
full operationalisation of the project is still a far cry. Though the Department claims that
there is no cost escalation so far, the Committee is convinced that the delay is certain to
entail cost overruns. The Committee gathers from the information furnished that out of
Rs. 64.50 crore allocated during the Eleventh Plan, Rs. 45.00 crore only could be utilized
which is indicative of the inefficient utilization of the budgeted funds. The Committee,
therefore, desires that an action plan be drawn for better deployment of the financial
resources during the Twelfth Plan so that any possibility of financial under-performance
could be obviated and there is no breach of the revised time-line of October, 2013 for the
operationalization of NEIAH. (Para 4.18)
North-Eastern Institute for Folk Medicine (NEIFM), Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh
The Committee is constrained to note the contradictions in the information furnished
by the Department. On the one hand, the Department claims that there is no proposal for
escalation of the cost estimate of the project, on the other, the approved outlay of Rs. 72.90
crore for the project gives an impression that the enhanced allocation has been made to
meet the cost overrun. The Committee, therefore, like the Department to explain this
apparent contradiction. (Para 4.21)
The Committee is also not happy with the tardy progress made towards
operationalisation of the project. A delay of more than three years have already taken
place, which is inordinate by any standard. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department streamline its monitoring mechanism and ensure that the revised time-line for
completion of the project is not extended in any event. The Committee desires to be
apprised of the steps taken to ensure timely implementation of this project. (Para 4.22)

34
The Committee observes that this project is intended to validate folk medicine
practices and integrate them into mainstream health care system. However, its
operationalisation in the true sense of the word can not be accomplished until the requisite
faculty and staff are appointed. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department
to proactively process the matter in the Integrated Finance Division and thereafter pursue
it with the Department of Expenditure. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the
progress made in this regard. (Para 4.24)
All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi
In its 55
th Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 26 th April, 2012, the Committee had
expressed its concern over the delay in implementation of this project and the resultant
time and cost overruns and recommended that a rigorous monitoring mechanism be put in
place to ensure execution of the project within the approved cost and designated time-line.
The Committee is constrained to note that despite the Department’s assurance made in past
that the project was on track, this project has witnessed time and cost overruns. The
Committee strongly disapproves of the Department’s failure to deliver the targeted outcome
within the designated time-line. The Committee only hopes that the Institute would be
operational at least during current financial year. (Para 4.27)
V . Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Development of AYUSH Institutions
The Committee does not understand as to why State Governments do not come
forward to get funds for strengthening the AYUSH colleges. The Department should make
an introspection in this regard and discuss with State Governments. (Para 5.4)
The Committee would recommend to the Department to expedite submission of the
report of the independent agency and find out the exact reasons for gross underutilization
of the budgeted amount under the above head and take corrective action accordingly by way
of making realistic projection of budgetary requirements and optimal utilization thereof.
The Committee would also like to be apprised of the findings of the independent agency and
action taken thereon. (Para 5.5)
The Committee observes that a substantial outlay of Rs. 450.00 crore has been
approved for the above scheme for the Twelfth Plan. The Committee would like the
Department to gear up its monitoring mechanism so as to avoid recurrence of such gross
financial underperformance as witnessed duing the Eleventh Plan. (Para 5.6)
VI. Assistance to Accredited AYUSH Centres of Excellence in Non-Governmental/Private
Sector Engaged in AYUSH Education/Drug Development
The Committee is constrained to observe that this is yet another instance of
unrealistic formulation of Budget Estimate and under utilization thereof. The Committee
disapproves of such unrealistic projection of fund requirements and impresses upon the
Department to ensure that such large variations in the Budget Estimates, Revised Estimates
and Actual Expenditure do not recur in future. (Para 6.6)
The Committee gathers from the information furnished that the Scheme is being
evaluated by an independent agency and would be modified as per its suggestions. The
Committee welcomes this exercise and desires to be apprised of the follow-up action taken
in this regard. (Para 6.7)
The Committee would also like to draw attention of the Department to the fact that
on the one hand, the Department has informed that the outlay for the Scheme for the

35
Twelfth Plan is Rs. 97.50 crore, on the other, the Outcome Budget 2013-14 States that the
Scheme was only for the Eleventh Plan and fresh proposal could be considered only on
approval of continuation of this Scheme. The Committee would, therefore, like the
Department to justify as to how such a huge amount of Rs. 97.50 crore is targeted to be
utilized if the continuation of the above Scheme is yet to be approved, though the first year
of the Twelfth Plan has already elapsed. When the experience in the Eleventh Plan shows
that there are very few eligible non-profit NGOs/Private Sector organizations in AYUSH,
then Department should better wind up the scheme. (Para 6.8)
VII. Research and Development including Medicinal Plants
The Committee notes that the outlay for the above head for the Twelfth Plan is
substantially higher than the Eleventh Plan allocations. A large number of important
activities are included under this head. The Committee is of the view that scientific
validation of classical formulations of Indian Systems of Medicine for their safety and
efficacy is of vital importance for promotion of these systems of medicine. The Committee,
therefore, desires that the Department should regularly monitor the utilization of allocated
funds under this head to ensure that the funds are utilized judiciously and the on-going
research activities are strengthened. (Para 7.2)
The Committee would also like to reiterate its recommendation made in its 55
th
Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 26 th April, 2012 that the Department should establish
a national registry of all AYUSH research studies and get the health outcomes accruing
from the research projects of the Research Councils evaluated by an independent agency.
The Committee desires to be apprised of the developments in this regard. (Para 7.3)
National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB)
The Committee is of the view that full-fledged SMPBs with full-time chief Executive
Officer will certainly lead to better implementation of the Schemes and programmes of
NMPB and more efficient deployment of financial resources. The Committee, therefore,
recommends to the Department to expedite its decision on increasing support for full
fledged SMPBs. (Para 7.8)
The Committee notes with concern that a substantial amount of Central funds for
the previous years continues to remain unaccounted for under both the schemes of NMPB
which is indicative of non-adherence to the basic financial norms. The Committee feels that
the delay in timely submission of UCs would adversely affect execution of the projects under
this head. The Committee would, therefore, recommend the Department to draw up a
concrete action plan for quicker liquidation of pending UCs within a designated time-line.
The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the measures taken and results achieved in
this regard. (Para 7.9)
The Committee has also been given to understand that an evaluation of the Schemes
of NMPB is going on and in the light of the suggestions made, the NMPB will be revised.
The Committee welcomes the ongoing evaluation of NMPB and desires to be kept apprised
of the suggestions made and action taken thereon. (Para 7.10)
The Committee notes that in pursuance of its recommendation, some progress has
been made towards filling up of the posts. The Committee would like to impress upon the
Department to vigorously pursue the matter and ensure that the remaining vacancies are
filled up within the shortest possible time. The Committee would like to be apprised of the
efforts made and results achieved in this regard. (Para 7.12)

36
VIII. Quality Control of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathic (ASU&H) Drugs
The Committee takes note of the steps taken by the Department for strengthening
of the regulatory mechanism of ASU&H drugs. However, the Committee is aware that
quality control and standardization of ASU&H drugs, which are mainly herbal/herbo-mineral
preparations, is very complex and different from synthetic molecules of the allopathic
system which are produced under controlled laboratory conditions. However, given the
current scenario where regulation of ASU&H drugs leaves much to be desired, the
Committee feels that strengthening and streamlining of regulatory mechanism of ASU&H
drugs needs to be speeded up. The Committee desires that the Department should accord
high priority to the task of laying down standards of quality control of ASU&H drugs by
using modern techniques. (Para 8.5)
The Committee observes that there is a separate chapter-IV A in the Drugs and
Cosmetics Act, 1940 which regulates the manufacture and sale of ASU drugs. Since the
enforcement of provisions of Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules made thereunder is under
the purview of State Drug Licensing and Drug Control Authorities, the state drugs
regulatory framework has a crucial role to play in ensuring safety and quality of ASU&H
drugs. It is in this context that strengthening of State Drug Testing Laboratories which are
facing infrastructure constraints, and shortage of manpower, assumes added significance.
The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department to quickly revise the Quality
Control Scheme and its funding pattern for greater efficacy of the Scheme. (Para 8.8)
Central Drug Controller for AYUSH
An early action may be taken to establish and appoint an AYUSH Drug Controller.
(Para 8.11)
IX. Central Sector Schemes for Development of AYUSH Industry Clusters
The Committee notes that 9 AYUSH Industry Clusters were set up during 2012-13.
It is a matter of concern that not a single new AYUSH Industry Cluster has been set up
since then which is indicative of the tardy progress in the matter. In its 55
th Report, the
Committee had suggested that there should be at least one AYUSH industry cluster in each
State. Though the Department has assured to move in this direction there is little action
on the ground. The Committee, therefore, exhorts the Department to quickly finalize
re-designing of the Scheme and ensure that concrete progress is made towards setting up
of at least one AYUSH Industry cluster in each State which is also necessary for supply of
quality drugs at affordable prices. (Para 9.5)
X. International Cooperation
The Committee notes that no MoUs have been signed or are in the process of being
signed with the developed countries like U.K, Germany, U.S.A, Canada etc. The Committee
observes that signing of MoUs for promotion of research projects of AYUSH with the
countries, which have well-developed and credible regulatory mechanisms, will go a long way
in establishing the therapeutic credential of AYUSH medicine globally. This needs to be
taken further ahead and India should become frontrunner in alternative systems of
medicine. (Para 10.3)
XI. Information, Education and Communication (IEC)
The Committee welcomes the evaluation of IEC and desires to be apprised of the
final findings of AFCL and the action taken thereon. (Para 11.4)

37
The Committee observes that no tangible progress has been made towards curtailing
misleading advertisements concerning AYUSH, over the electronic media and in the print
media. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should pursue the
matter with the authorities concerned with renewed vigour as the issue is too important for
maintaining credibility of AYUSH systems to be left unattended. The Committee desires to
be apprised of the final outcome in the matter. (Para 11.7)
XII. Miscellaneous
The Committee observes that 20 yoga therapy Centres were targeted to be set up in
AYUSH/Allopathy hospitals during the Eleventh Plan, but only 6 such centres could be set
up during the Plan period. The Committee expresses its displeasure over this sorry state of
affairs and strongly recommends that such yoga therapy centres be set in all AYUSH/
Allopathy hospitals all over the country during the current Plan period. The Committee
would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard. (Para 12.1)
The Committee also observes that during the Eleventh Plan, 150 tours for
documentation of reported cases of prevention/treatment of vector-borne/infectious diseases
by Siddha Drugs were targeted; however, only 31 tours could be conducted. The Committee
is of the view that there is an urgent need for improvement in documentation of the
reported episodes of prevention/treatment of vector-born infectious diseases by Siddha drugs
and recommends that the Department should make all out efforts to complete
documentation of all the reported cases of prevention/treatment/cure of vector-borne/
infectious diseases not only by Siddha drugs but also by Ayurvedic and other traditional
drugs. (Para 12.2)

REPORT
I. Introduction
1.1 The Department of Health Research was created in the Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare in 2007 and became functional in November, 2008 with appointment of the first Secretary,
who is also the DG, Indian Council for Medical Research (ICMR).
The following work has been allocated to the Department of Health Research:
1. Promotion and co-ordination of basic, applied and clinical research including clinical
trials and operational research in areas related to medical, health, biomedical and
medical profession and education through development of infrastructure, manpower
and skills in cutting edge areas and management of related information thereto.
2. Promote and provide guidance on research governance issues, including ethical issues
in medical and health research.
3. Inter-sectoral coordination and promotion of public-private-spartnership in medical,
biomedical and health research related areas.
4. Advanced training in research areas concerning medicine and health, including grant of
fellowships for such training in India and abroad.
5. International co-operation in medical and health research, including work related to
international conferences in related areas in India and abroad.
6. Technical support for dealing with epidemics and natural calamities.
7. Investigation of outbreaks due to new and exotic agents and development of tools for
prevention.
8. Matters relating to scientific societies and associations, charitable and religious
endowments in medicine and health research areas.
9. Coordination between organizations and institutes under the Central and State
Governments in areas related to the subjects entrusted to the Department and for the
promotion of special studies in medicine and health.
10. Administering and monitoring of Indian Council of Medical Research.
1.2 The Department has informed that the work relating to Indian Council of Medical Research
(ICMR) was the only on-going scheme to have been transferred to the Department and other nine
functions are new.
1.3 As per the information given in the Outcome Budget 2013-14, five new schemes have been
formulated so as to fulfill the mandate and work entrusted to the Department and efforts are
underway to secure mandatory clearances for them:–
The Schemes are:–
(i) Human Resource Development for Health Research
(ii) Grants-in-Aid Scheme for Inter-sectoral Convergence and Promotion and Guidance on
Research Governance Issues

2
(iii) Establishment of Multi-Disciplinary Research Units (MRUs) in Government Medical
Colleges under the initiative of Infrastructure Development for Health Research
(iv) Establishment of Model Rural Health Research Units (MRHRUs) in the States Colleges
under the initiative of Infrastructure Development for Health Research
(v) Establishment of a network of Laboratories for Managing Epidemics and Natural
Calamities.

2.6 The Committee observes that the five new schemes/projects of the Department of
Health Research could not be made operational even during 2012-13 due to lack of
approvals, though the Department had come into existence in 2007 and become functional
in 2008 with the appointment of its first Secretary. The Committee is unable to comprehend
the reasons for not getting the required approvals even after a lapse of five years since the
creation of the Department, which has resulted in massive financial underperformance vis-
à-vis the approved outlay of Rs. 4496.08 crore for the Eleventh Plan. The Committee has
been exhorting the Department to pay focused attention for completing all pre-project
formalities and obtaining necessary approvals on time so that the budgeted funds are not
locked up for want of approvals and surrendered later. The Committee is, however,
constrained to note that little attention seems to have been paid to its advice in this regard
which has resulted in persistent and substantial under-utilisation of budgeted funds. The
first year of the Twelfth Plan Period has already elapsed and the current year is the 2nd
year of the Twelfth Plan. The Committee notes that the EFC approval for the three new
Schemes were accorded, albeit belatedly, on 22.03.2013. Two of the five new schemes have
not been approved as yet. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department to
make more rigorous efforts and proactively pursue approval of the remaining two schemes
with the agencies concerned. The Committee desires to be apprised of the updated status
in this regard. The Committee also recommends that a roadmap be chalked out to
implement the Schemes and progress of their implementation be monitored at highest level
in the Department so that the desired outcomes are achieved. The Committee desires that
all the approved schemes should be made operational at least during current financial year.
Approvals to the remaining schemes may be accorded at the earliest so that they may also
become operational during the current year.
2.7 The Committee notes that there is significant variation between the Budget
Estimates and the actual expenditure incurred in respect of the five new schemes of the
Department. Persistent mismatch between the Budget Estimates and the actual expenditure
indicates that budget formulation is being done without applying proper financial yardsticks.
The Committee feels that there is an imperative need to minimize the huge mismatch
between the Budget Estimates and the actual expenditure so as to observe the fiscal norms
in letter and spirit. The Committee, therefore, recommends that corrective measures be
initiated and implemented for realistic projection of fund requirements of the Department
in future.
2.8 Highlighting the reduced allocation of Rs. 726.00 crore under plan head for 2013-14 against
the projected demand of Rs. 2283.00 crore, the Department has stated that this reduction in the
allocation will affect almost all the on-going as well as new schemes. While the ICMR will not be
able to approve new extramural projects at desired level and will have to delay initiation of the new
programmes for which SFC/EFC have already been approved or under progress, physical targets

6
of the new schemes of the DHR will have to be curtailed quantitatively to nearly 40 per cent. The
Department has informed that it proposes to request for adequate funds at the RE stage.
2.9 The Secretary during the course of his deposition before the Committee reiterated the fact
that the reduced allocation for 2013-14 would adversely affect the physical targets proposed in the
five new schemes of DHR and result in curtailment of several on-going and new intramural and
extramural research programmes of ICMR. Specifying the activities to be affected adversely due
to the less allocation for 2013-14, the Secretary stated the following:–
• Setting up/strengthening of various centers of ICMR (EFC approved/in process).
• New Research Programmes in gap areas including bone health, allergy, mental health,
oral health, socio-behavioural health.
• Research on Tribal, Marginalized/ unprivileged population.
• Special Programmes for Medical Colleges and strengthening infrastructure.
• Research on issues related to Bhopal gas tragedy.
2.10 The Committee observes that scientific knowledge generated through health and bio-
medical research is used to develop drugs, diagnostics, vaccines and devices that ultimately
find place in the health care systems of the country. It is also worth mentioning that health
research has a vital role to play in the discovery and development of indigenous health
products. Taking all these factors into account, the Committee apprehends that allowing the
new schemes to be plagued with under-funding from the very beginning would prove
detrimental to generation of new knowledge in the area of health research. The Committee,
therefore, lends its support for enhancement of funds for the schemes at the RE stage. The
Committee, simultaneously, recommends to the Department to pay focused attention to
more efficient deployment of the available resources.
2.11 In reply to a question, the Department has informed that out of the approved outlay of
Rs. 10029.00 crore (against the projected demand for Rs. 15,500.00 crore), for the Twelfth Plan,
an allocation of Rs. 5229.00 crore has been earmarked for new schemes/programmes of the
Department and that this would by and large suffice to meet the requirements for implementation
of the 5 new schemes.
2.12 As regards the programmes of ICMR, there will be curtailment of some of its Plans such
as establishment of new Centres in gap areas (many of which are at advanced stages of processing
for seeking approvals) and also extramural grants to various medical and research institutions. The
Department will request for more money after the appropriate mid-term review of the progress of
its programmes and activities.
2.13 The Committee observes that the ICMR is the main technical wing of the
Department of Health Research and is responsible for formulation, coordination and
promotion of bio-medical research in the country. The Committee, therefore, notes with
serious concern the likely adverse impact of the funds crunch on the intramural and
extramural research priorities of ICMR. The Committee desires that Planning Commission/
Ministry of Finance may reconsider the allocation for ICMR for the Twelfth Plan after
making a fair assessment.
III. Indian Council of Medical Research
3.1 As per the information given in the Annual Report of the Department, the ICMR
concentrates on knowledge generation and affordable technology development and serves as the
fulcrum of the Department.

7

th April, 2013 submitted the following:–

3.3 The Committee places on record its appreciation for the achievements of ICMR
during the Eleventh Plan. However, in view of the dynamic international health research
scenario and the current and future health challenges of the country, the ICMR has an
uphill task to accomplish and milestones to achieve. The Committee would, therefore, like
the ICMR to collaborate with internationally acclaimed institutions in the field of Health

VII. Development of Infrastructure for Promotion of Health Research
7.1 As per the information given in the Outcome Budget 2013-14, development of infrastructure
for research has been taken up as a major activity of Department of Health Research. During
2013-14 it is proposed to establish about 60 Multidisciplinary Research Units (MRU) in medical
colleges and 10 model Rural Health Research Units (MRHRU); 10-15 specialized research
laboratories in cutting edge areas as well as trans-disciplinary aspects involving agencies like
AYUSH, NKN etc.
7.2 (i) Establishment of Multi-Disciplinary Research Units (MRUs)
• Medical colleges are the backbone of both teaching as well as providing specialized
services to patients in India. It is also expected that medical colleges will also set the
trends in thinking process and innovation to improve our understanding of the
disease(s) and their management.
• Over the years it has been seen that majority of our medical colleges are just confining
to routine patient care and also teaching based on conventional methods. This is
thought to be basically because of lack of appropriate facilities and even lack of
adequate attempt to create such new facilities e.g. modern biology units in the medical
colleges. As a result, medical colleges even do not think of including the new methods
of investigation for understanding the patho-biology, diagnosis, treatment and/or
monitoring the progress of cases for better management practices. The Department of
Health Research plans to pay special attention to development of infrastructure in
medical colleges by establishing multi-disciplinary research units (around 150 units in
Twelfth Plan) at least in all the Government medical colleges. These units will provide
the modern technology infrastructure which will improve the quality of the specialized
care, training of doctors and other health care professionals and then research as per
the needs of the population. About sixty medical colleges have applied/been identified
by State Governments and these Units are planned to be established in 2013-14 after
completing the formalities.
7.3 Development of infrastructure for research has been taken up as a major activity of
Department of Health Research. During 2013-14 it is proposed to establish about 60 Multi-
disciplinary Research Units (MRU) in medical colleges. The Committee was given to understand
that the Department of Health Research’s Technical Committee has shortlisted 31 Medical Colleges
in 14 different States for establishing Multi-Disciplinary Research Units (MRUs). However, not a
single MRU is being set up in Bihar, inspite of the fact that Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital
had submitted a proposal for the same .
7.4 The Committee, therefore, recommends that the proposal of Darbhanga Medical
College and Hospital for establishing MRU may also be considered for approval and a MRU
be set up there at the earliest.

17
(ii) Establishment of Model Rural Health Research Units (MRHRU):
7.5 There is a wide gap between the available specialized health care technology and the
technology being developed vis-a-vis their utilization in the State health systems. This is particularly
true for rural health settings. It is generally felt that technology application needs specialized
infrastructure and can be done only in urban settings. In order to develop models for transfer of
such technology to the end care users, the Department has planned to establish model rural health
research units in all the States (about 50); one in smaller States and more than one in larger States)
where technology transfer and the research targeting health interventions will be done in partnership
with the States. It has been planned to establish 10 units by the end of 2013-14.
7.6 The Committee observes that though first year of the Twelfth Plan has already
elapsed and the 2
nd Year has started, no MRU or MRHRU has been set up till date. From

VIII. Managing Epidemics and National Calamities
Setting up a Laboratory Network for Research on Viral and other Infectious Diseases.
8.1 As per the information furnished by the Department, India continues to have outbreaks/
epidemics due to various infectious pathogens. Currently national apex institutes like NCDC, New
Delhi and NIV , Pune are mandated to undertake the investigations that results in heavy burden
affecting their real referral role. The resultant delay in diagnosis/detection and adequate/incomplete
data about these outbreaks significantly impacts the response time for interventions. Significantly,
avoidable delays in both short and long terms strategies for prevention, treatment through vaccine
production/introduction and up-gradation of infra-structure etc. The Department has planned to
establish about 250 laboratories (total in 3-4 years) of three grades on infectious pathogens which
will work under the overall guidance of apex institutions like NIV, NCDC through appropriate
linkages and networking. During 2013-14 it is planned to establish 2 regional BSL-III; 14 State level
labs and 70 district level labs.
8.2 The Committee observes that viral diagnosis has emerged as a major health
challenge. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should draw up an
action plan for timely implementation of the scheme for setting up of laboratory network
for research on viral and other infections. Efforts may be made to achieve physical and
financial targets.

1. Joint Secretary: An officer of Indian Forest Service has been selected by Department
of Personnel and Training (DoPT). He will report for duty on 7
th March, 2013.
2. Scientists: For the post of Scientist ‘C’ and Scientist ‘E’, the posts can be filled only
after the Recruitment Rules are approved by the DoPT and UPSC.
3. Secretariat Posts: The Central Secretariat posts have been encadered by the Department
of Personnel and Training in July, 2012, against some posts, postings of which are yet
to be made by the DoPT. Moreover, the cadre controlling authority for the DHR is the
Department of Health and Family Welfare and, therefore, actual posting of officers are
first made by the DoPT to that department thereafter the officers are posted by that
Department to the DHR. Department of Health and Family Welfare has been reminded
in September, 2012 and January, 2013 for early posting of requisite staff in the DHR
against the sanctioned posts. However, as a stop gap arrangement, two Consultants
(one Retired Director and One Retired Under Secretary) have been engaged for
handling the important work, including the work relating to the schemes.
10.3 The Committee notes that despite coming into existence of DHR as a separate
Department in 2007, the cadre-controlling authority for the DHR is the Department of
Health and Family Welfare. The purpose being served by having such an arrangement is
beyond the comprehension of the Committee. The Committee feels that such an
arrangement would only delay the process of filling up of vacant posts and should,
therefore, be dispensed with. The Committee would therefore, like the Department of
Health Research to bring the above observation to the notice of the authorities concerned

20
for an appropriate decision. The Committee desires to be apprised of the response of
Department of Health and Family Welfare in this regard.
10.4 The Committee also expresses its concern over a large number of posts lying vacant
vis-à-vis the sanctioned strength, which is certain to impinge on the smooth functioning of
the Department. The Committee would recommend that the matter should be pursued at
the highest level with the concerned authorities for expeditious filling up of the vaccines at
the earliest. A Department cannot function with so many vacancies. If the government did
not create a separate Department, things would have been different. But now that the
Government has created the Department, all the commitments should be fulfilled. An early
action may be taken in this regard.

21
OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
II. Budgetary Allocation
The Committee observes that the five new schemes/projects of the Department of
Health Research could not be made operational even during 2012-13 due to lack of
approvals, though the Department had come into existence in 2007 and become functional
in 2008 with the appointment of its first Secretary. The Committee is unable to comprehend
the reasons for not getting the required approvals even after a lapse of five years since the
creation of the Department, which has resulted in massive financial under-performance
vis-a-vis the approved outlay of Rs.4496.08 crore for the Eleventh Plan. The Committee has
been exhorting the Department to pay focused attention for completing all pre-project
formalities and obtaining necessary approvals on time so that the budgeted funds are not
locked up for want of approvals and surrendered later. The Committee is, however,
constrained to note that little attention seems to have been paid to its advice in this regard
which has resulted in persistent and substantial under-utilisation of budgeted funds. The
first year of the Twelfth Plan Period has already elapsed and the current year is the 2
nd year
of the Twelfth Plan. The Committee notes that the EFC approval for the three new Schemes
were accorded, albeit belatedly, on 22.03.2013. Two of the five new schemes have not been
approved as yet. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department to make more
rigorous efforts and proactively pursue approval of the remaining two schemes with the
agencies concerned. The Committee desires to be apprised of the updated status in this
regard. The Committee also recommends that a roadmap be chalked out to implement the
Schemes and progress of their implementation be monitored at highest level in the
Department so that the desired outcomes are achieved. The Committee desires that all the
approved schemes should be made operational at least during current financial year.
Approvals to the remaining schemes may be accorded at the earliest so that they may also
become operational during the current year. (Para 2.6)
The Committee notes that there is significant variation between the Budget
Estimates and the actual expenditure incurred in respect of the five new schemes of the
Department. Persistent mismatch between the Budget Estimates and the actual expenditure
indicates that budget formulation is being done without applying proper financial yardsticks.
The Committee feels that there is an imperative need to minimize the huge mismatch
between the Budget Estimates and the actual expenditure so as to observe the fiscal norms
in letter and spirit. The Committee, therefore, recommends that corrective measures be
initiated and implemented for realistic projection of fund requirements of the Department
in future. (Para 2.7)
The Committee observes that scientific knowledge generated through health and bio-
medical research is used to develop drugs, diagnostics, vaccines and devices that ultimately
find place in the health care systems of the country. It is also worth mentioning that health
research has a vital role to play in the discovery and development of indigenous health
products. Taking all these factors into account, the Committee apprehends that allowing the
new schemes to be plagued with under-funding from the very beginning would prove
detrimental to generation of new knowledge in the area of health research. The Committee,
therefore, lends its support for enhancement of funds for the schemes at the RE stage. The
21

22
Committee, simultaneously, recommends to the Department to pay focused attention to
more efficient deployment of the available resources. (Para 2.10)
The Committee observes that the ICMR is the main technical wing of the
Department of Health Research and is responsible for formulation, coordination and
promotion of bio-medical research in the country. The Committee, therefore, notes with
serious concern the likely adverse impact of the funds crunch on the intramural and
extramural research priorities of ICMR. The Committee desires that Planning Commission/
Ministry of Finance may reconsider the allocation for ICMR for the Twelfth  Plan after
making a fair assessment. (Para 2.13)
III. Indian Council of Medical Research
The Committee places on record its appreciation for the achievements of ICMR
during the Eleventh Plan. However, in view of the dynamic international health research
scenario and the current and future health challenges of the country, the ICMR has an
uphill task to accomplish and milestones to achieve. The Committee would, therefore, like
the ICMR to collaborate with internationally acclaimed institutions in the field of Health
research in order to facilitate a vibrant and relevant health research system in the country.
(Para 3.3)
The Committee welcomes the on-going evaluation of the research activities of ICMR
by an independent Committee. The Committee would Impress upon the Department to
expedite submission of the recommendations of the independent Committee and place them
in the public domain. The Committee desires to be apprised of the composition, findings of
the independent Committee and the follow-up action taken thereon. The Committee would
also like to know if it is possible to involve reputed scholars of developed countries in the
evaluation of the research projects of ICMR. (Para 3.5)
The Committee notes that some very important research activities/projects in varied
areas are targeted to be undertaken/continued during the year 2013-14. The Committee
would like to be apprised in due course of time, of the quantifiable and specific
achievements made vis-à-vis targets set for the year 2013-14. (Para 3.7)
The Committee notes that a number of outcomes have been projected for the year
2013-14. The Committee recommends that the desired outcomes be achieved within the
targeted time-frame. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the achievements made
vis-a-vis  the targets set. The Committee observes that it takes time to translate the
research leads into tangible health products or in application of the knowledge generated
through research and a lot of work remains to be done to bridge the gap between ‘what is
known’ and ‘what is done’. Concerted efforts are required to be made to bring research
outcomes into application in the better interest of the public. The Committee would,
therefore, like to be apprised of the finding of the Committee constituted to identify the
leads from the completed extramural research projects. The Committee would also like to
be intimated of the specific health products/processes accruing from the above research
projects. (Para 3.10)
ICMR – NIF joint collaborative programme in traditional practices
The Committee observes that no single system of health care has the capacity to
solve all of the country’s health care needs. It is in this context that promotion of research
in the area of traditional medicines including Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Tibbia, Sowa-Rigpa and
Homoeopathy becomes vital for the public health care system. The Committee, therefore,

23
recommends that the research projects on traditional medicines be pursued vigorously and
the innovations accruing therefrom be introduced into public health service within a
designated time-frame. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the success achieved
in this regard. (Para 3.17)
IV. Programmes for the North East
The Committee welcomes the initiatives taken by the Department to undertake
studies and projects specific to North Eastern Region and exhorts that focused attention be
paid to the implementation of the above projects by way of streamlined monitoring so that
tangible outcomes could be achieved and benefits emerging therefrom percolate down to the
people. (Para 4.3)
V . Human Resource Development for Health Research
The Committee observes that much delay has already taken place in implementing
the schemes pertaining to Human Resource Development which resulted in the surrender
of the entire budgeted funds for 2012-13. The Committee would expect the Department to
avoid recurrence of such a situation and get the EFC clearance at the earliest. The
Committee would also like the Department to complete other pre-project activities within
the shortest possible time. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the development
in this regard. (Para 5.5)
VI. Grant-in-Aid Schemes for Inter-Sectoral Convergence and Promotion and Guidance
on Research Governance Issues
The Committee gathers from the information furnished that the Grant in Aid
Scheme for Inter-Sectoral Convergence and Promotion and Guidance on Research
Governance Issues is yet to be cleared by the EFC/Cabinet. The Committee, in the earlier
part of the Report, has commented about proactively pursuing for approval of various
Schemes with the agencies concerned and completing all pre-project formalities well in time.
The Committee recommends here also to take similar action in respect of the above
Scheme as well. (Para 6.2)
Grant-in-Aid scheme for projects requiring inter-sectoral coordination, translation
specially in PPP mode and IT enabled governance, trans-disciplinary as well as
implementation research.
The Committee observes that very important activities are envisaged to be
accomplished under the Grant in Aid Scheme for Inter-Sectoral Convergence and Promotion
and Guidance on Research Governance Issues. The Committee in its 56
th Report on

accomplishment of targets set under the Scheme would require involvement of a number of

The Committee is not aware whether such a dispensation has come into existence or not.
The Committee, therefore, would like to be updated in this regard. (Para 6.6)
Promotion and Guidance on Research Governance Issues
The Committee recommends that early action be taken for setting up MTDB which
will go a long way in promoting development of indigenous medical technologies. (Para 6.9)

Multi-disciplinary Research Units (MRUs)

Establishment of Model Rural Health Research Units (MRHRUs)

nd Year has started, no MRU or MRHRU has been set up till date. From

Setting up a Laboratory Network for Research on Viral and other Infectious Diseases.
The Committee observes that viral diagnosis has emerged as a major health
